branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Progressive Localized Cutaneous Lesion with Solid Nodule and Dilated Lymphatic Vessels

state.case_summary:
A previously healthy 16-year-old girl presented with a red tumor on her right upper arm that enlarged over 6 months. The lesion initially started as a small cutaneous nodule without obvious triggers that gradually developed and enlarged to form a red-colored tumor with a hard nodule inside. There was no history of local trauma or insect bite. Her personal, past, and family histories were unremarkable.

There was a 6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor on the right upper arm, which extended 1 to 3 cm from the epidermal surface. Inside the tumor, a nontender, firm-to-hard nodule was palpated. There was no regional lymphadenopathy, and results of the rest of the physical and systemic examinations were normal.

- Laboratory tests: Hematologic, biochemical, and urinalysis tests were normal.- Pathological examination:  Image Title: Excisional tumor gross specimen  Image Description: Showed multilocular spaces below the epidermis and a solid tumor present in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance  Image Title: Histological examination  Image Description: Revealed basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor

excluded_candidates: Inflammatory or infectious process: lack of systemic symptoms and normal laboratory tests
Traumatic or reactive process: no history of local trauma or insect bite
